As a daily Bitbucket user, browsing source code via web is painful and slow compared to Github's slicker UI with tree slider navigation.
Bitbucket's primary advantage over GitHub is unlimited private repositories with cost based on collaborators, not repo count.
GitHub completely trounces Bitbucket with their ease of use and toolset. I hope Bitbucket can step it up.
I have to authenticate every time I push to the repo despite adding my SSH key; can't find equivalent to github.user/github.token config for Bitbucket.
None of my existing Bitbucket repos have a Git link, nor can I find a way to add Git support from the Admin screen, only for new repos.
The readme is now narrow and can't expand; my <pre> text is much too wide and shows scrollbars. No whitespace around h3/h1/h2 headers, looks cramped.
The redesigned commits view is 100 times better than Github's ever was - so much more info, and even a graph like in gitx.
GitLab is FOSS and already has almost all of these features, allowing multiple private repos on a single cheap VPS - that's why I chose it over Bitbucket or Github.
So how do I browse projects hosted on BitBucket? No search feature by language, no Explore feature like GitHub - can't test drive before signing up.
Github's UI has been slowly getting worse over the last year, and their paid account options are terrible with limits on number of private repos rather than disk space.
Another place GitHub is dropping the ball is the social aspect - terrible activity feeds I can't believe anyone uses.
I recently stopped paying $12/month for github and moved all my private repositories to bitbucket. Since it's just me, it's totally free.
I use Bitbucket at work. And it stinks compared to Github.
I love bitbucket but I would like to be able to create clusters of related projects by language/tool. Right now there isn't even a search feature, let alone browse capability.
GitHub charges per repo whereas Bitbucket charges per user - GitHub makes sense for few repos, Bitbucket is more cost effective for agencies with a repo per client.
Bitbucket's deploy key is read-only and can be attached to multiple repos, unlike Github's which is read-write and single-repo only - a much better fit for typical deploy key use.
I tried sourcehut but found the pull request flow confusing - there aren't actual pull requests but instead some email flow that I didn't have time to figure out.
This is disappointing. Bitbucket is the premier place to host free private mercurial repos - there is literally not a single other place for free private hosting.
It appears that in bitbucket enterprise cloud, there is no way for an administrator to prevent members of my team from making repositories public to the Internet.

June 1 2020: all Mercurial repositories will be removed. Is BitBucket really that pressed for disk space? I hope they will reconsider and move those repos to a read-only archive instead of obliterating them.
